utterances.text: No. No. No. Please, there was a statement in Celebici. That was the first one. The second one was in the court in Belgrade. The third one in Timosoira and then the fourth one in Belgrade. Those are the four statements.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I have four -- I have enough statements here, so I would like to have the witness be given this statement with his own signature and I have additional copies for the Prosecution and for the Trial Chamber. (Handed). The second statement, which can be given to the witness is the one given to the military commission of the 4th Corps in Konjic. While this is being processed, Mr. Dordic, as you confirmed, you were in buildings Number 6, Number 9. You were interrogated in the administration building and across from it was Building Number 22, and later you also said that you were unloading some things in the building where the logistics centre of the army was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but that was just food and weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, you know the Celebici camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I became familiar with it while I was there.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So the structure that we see there, this is over a square area that is several thousand square metres large?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And there are significant logistical facilities of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina that are housed there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: With respect to the period of time that you spent in Celebici, you must have seen that a number of trucks arrived there as well as personnel, people that you didn't know, and people who had something to do with the delivery of food supplies and other stuff to these barracks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, can you please look at the statement from Celebici and see if this is your signature?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is probably my handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you please look at the statement dated 12/1/1993, for which you told my colleague McMurrey that you remembered it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Hold on. I think that we had a big misunderstanding a while ago. I think you said the statement from Musala.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What I meant was at that time you were at Musala?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then we did not understand each other. What I said is that I gave a statement in Celebici. I do not deny that, but I did not give any statement in Musala.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, the other statement. Maybe the place where you gave it is a different place, but at that time you were at Musala. Is this your signature?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. But I don't recall this statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Actually what he says about these four statements doesn't make any difference. If these statements were made, they were made. Except you want to contradict him on any of the statements, there's no need for pressing the number of statements he made. It's your case. I'm not interfering with the way you conduct it. I don't see any benefit from this. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): You were, the witness stated correctly how many times he gave statements and answered questions regarding the criminal proceedings against him. Since these documents speak to other matters, I wanted for the credibility of the witness' sake as well as other questions, and I only have a few more questions here, I just wanted to complete the identification of all the statements that he had given. Mr. Dordic in your statement before the judge from Belgrade you said that you were interrogated by some policemen from Sarajevo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the time you wrote a statement without any coercion; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I didn't make any statement. We just spoke about some things that had happened after we were detained.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can I show the witness for the sake of identification his statement of 6th June 1993?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, show it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: The Prosecution would like a copy also: MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): A copy for the witness. (Handed). Do you recall this statement, Mr. Dordic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just a moment, please: (Pause). It looks like my handwriting but I can't recall at this moment whom I gave this statement to.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But you recognise your signature and your handwriting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It looks like mine, which doesn't mean to say that it cannot be a forgery.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you aware of the fact that criminal charges were brought against you before the military Tribunal, department of Konjic, for unauthorised possession of weapons and for participation in an enemy army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the military Prosecutor instructed the beginning of investigations against you for the same offences?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware, Mr. Dordic, that you were pardoned for the sake of exchange?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I know only of one person for whom abolition arrived for the sake of exchange and that is Stravko Dordic.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You know that criminal proceedings were conducted against Stravko Dordic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, the documents of the military Tribunal in Konjic, you are not familiar with them if they do exist?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would now like to ask you your Honours for the document -- the statements from Celebici and Musala which have been identified by the witness to be admitted as defence exhibits?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: The Prosecution's first question would be for what purpose are they being admitted, and the Prosecution will note they had not been provided with copies of any of these documents beforehand. So before we take a position as to whether or not we object to their admission, we would like to know the purpose for which they are sought to be admitted. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): For the purpose of identification. I gave them for identification but they are being admitted for the purpose of impeachment of the witness and, secondly, this evidence was not conveyed to the Prosecution beforehand, because our obligation applies. If we have an identified document and if we wish to use it as evidence, then we are obliged to give it to the Prosecution, as we have done immediately after the identification of the document by the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will certainly note that I don't believe the discovery rules which provide that defence counsel must give reciprocal discovery envisions that it will happen in the few seconds before it is given to the witness. So I certainly would object for that ground and I will note that we have noted this has been a continuing problem and we previously noted that we would object to any future ones. In fact, before this witness was cross-examined I went to defence counsel and said: "Are there any documents going to be shown to this witness?" Again I was not given any of these documents. I would also note that I don't believe these documents are proper impeachment, so we would object on that ground also.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Frankly I did not even notice any impeachment circumstances there, because I did not see any contradiction which was pointed out in the statements which were tendered. So I don't see how it stands for impeachment. It does not. There is no basis for tendering it. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): I must state, first of all, that the Prosecution did not ask us, as defence counsel of Zejnil Delalic, for any documents beforehand and the Trial Chamber has already been in a situation to accept a document in the possession of the defence shown to the witness for the purpose of surprise. When he identifies it, it is of significance to us and we then supply a copy to the Prosecution. We have acted in an identical manner this time. Secondly, in both these statements reference is made to the participation of this witness in disarming two TO members and in the killing of or in the death of a TO member, and that is the contradiction between his testimony and the documents he has identified.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "Will you please tell me which killing you are referring to?", says the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: I don't know what is going on, why is evidence continuing while you are making the address. Now you are telling us why these documents should be admitted for impeachment purposes. As I said, there is nothing in his statement and the evidence which he has tendered which contradicts them, because he has not denied much of the things that he has made in his statement. That has not been denied. I don't see the basis for it: how are the statements you have tendered even suggesting to him. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Your Honours, in that case I propose that the documents remain for identification purposes and defence counsel, if necessary, will later submit these documents as evidence, since the witness has already identified his handwriting and his signature?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I apologise, your Honours. I said that this looks like my signature but that it need not be a forgery.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: It can be tendered as identification, I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: For identification purposes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no objection to it being part of the record. As I understand it, all documents shown to a witness, whether adopted or not adopted, are made part of the record that they were identified. Now I will clarify that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Apart from that, in this specific case he has not denied that this is his signature. He has not denied that, so he could not -- and he has identified the document as looking like his own handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: That is right. I understand that he has -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: The question is whether actually he made it, because it is not addressed to anybody. So I don't see how -- to who he made his statement and in what circumstances it was made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: That you will prove. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Yes, we will prove that in the continuation of these proceedings. Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: I think I only have two questions.

utterances.speaker: MISS MCHENRY
utterances.text: Sir, Mr. Dordic, in January of 1993 were you ever interrogated in the presence of five people as well as Ismeta Pozdor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as Ismeta is concerned, I was questioned only on the first day I was brought to Celebici camp. I remember that woman from that day. I said that there was just Niksic and Stenek. I don't remember five people.

utterances.speaker: MISS MCHENRY
utterances.text: Okay. And that's correct. I believe you have identified one statement in June -- that you gave in Celebici. I am asking whether or not in January 1993 you remember being brought in front of a different group, which included Ismeta Pozdor as well as five other persons in January of 1993?

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I rather think that she is beginning to -- excuse me, please. I rather think my learned friend is beginning to suggest the answer she requires from a witness. That in any system of law is a leading question, not a question in re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: They will prove the document and then you may question it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: I know they may. Especially with respect to these documents we have had problems before, and given that I'm not -- I don't believe they are going to be able to prove up this document. I just want the record to be clear as to what this witness does. I am not going to ask him any more questions other than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Except you want to show that he really meant --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Except you want to show that he made this statement and he made it to someone, which is still lacking in the document, I don't see why you should bother about any statement, any questions at this stage.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Okay. Just my final question. Sir, are you in a position to be able to recognise Mr. Esad Landzo's handwriting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS MCHENRY
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: I think that's all we have for this witness. We are adjourning today and resuming on Monday, 23rd June at 2.00 pm I think for the video conference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: --ooOoo--

procedural_notes.text: (Hearing adjourned until Monday, 23rd June at 2.00 pm)
